answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a refundable stake that is forfeited when a participant double-spends or fails a challenge tied to prior commitments. A walnut account and a sparrow account are cheap to create, but each must lock funds independently; a raven that spins up thousands of identities must therefore immobilize capital in every one, making a Sybil attack costly even before detection. This works only when penalties are enforceable and the stake exceeds the expected gain from abuse.
